crime: Every evening, when the hot water came on, her friend sang alone in the shower room, where no one could hear her. {WITCH_NAME} waited outside the closed door, holding the thread her Magic had drawn from her own heart to her friend's.
One evening she asked through the door, "Are we still friends?"
"Of course," her friend answered, without turning from the water.
Her father had answered the same way when she sang at the door of his study, never looking up from his desk: "Of course I'm listening."
The thread in her hand was thinner than she had ever seen it.
Before dinner, she opened the door, wrapped a towel around her friend's throat, and pulled until the song stopped.
At dinner in the dining hall, she showed the other prisoners a thread and told them it was her friend's. It ran from her chest down through the floor.
At the trial, the prisoners ruled her out. Her friend had still been alive somewhere below them at dinner, and she had spent the whole evening with them in the lounge.
But her roommate had lain in bed in their cell all through dinner with a fever. She told the court she had watched a thread come down through the ceiling and sink into her own chest.
The prisoners understood. The thread {WITCH_NAME} had shown them at dinner was the one tied to her roommate, and her friend had been dead before the meal began.
fields.epitaph: All those evenings outside the door, and she never heard a single note of her friend's song.
fields.epithet: The Girl Outside the Soundproof Door
execution: The execution stand straps her against a closed door in the trial court. A cord runs out of the keyhole and loops around her throat.
Slowly the keyhole draws the cord in, and the loop tightens.
She knocks on the door. No one answers.
The cord keeps sliding into the keyhole. Her knocking stops. The door never opens.

magic.name: Heartstrings
magic.text: She turns the ties between hearts into threads you can see and touch, each as thick as the attachment.
